A Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping based on the conditional distributions of initial separations at fixed present-day separation, measured directly from the simulations, allows the model to reproduce the overall trends in both real and redshift space without additional fitting. The hydrodynamic and DM-only runs generally show similar DM halo spin-axis correlations, although the DM-only run exhibits a steeper rise at small real-space separations. In the hydrodynamic run, stellar spin-axis correlations are consistent with the same Lagrangian form as their DM halo counterparts, but with approximately 60% of the DM correlation amplitudes. Positive stellar correlations persist in both real and redshift space, and the mapped model captures their separation dependence. Initial spin-axis correlations of protohalos are substantially stronger than their present-day counterparts at the same Lagrangian separations, consistent with subsequent nonlinear spin evolution weakening these correlations. These results suggest that present-day halo and stellar spin-axis correlations retain signatures of the initial tidal field and that their general behavior can be understood through LTTT-based modeling combined with pair-separation mapping.

papers.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
papers.summary: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

papers.title: SysBio-SR: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression for Trajectory Fidelity and Mechanism Recovery in Systems Biology
papers.summary: Symbolic regression seeks to discover interpretable governing equations for dynamical systems from data. In systems biology, however, accurately reproducing system trajectories does not necessarily imply recovery of the underlying reaction mechanisms. Existing benchmarks evaluate numerical accuracy, expression complexity, or equation-level similarity, but not agreement between recovered reactions and reference mechanisms in biological systems. We introduce SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems with reaction annotations spanning mass action, Michaelis--Menten, Hill, and complex kinetics. Trajectory fidelity is evaluated across all systems under in-distribution reconstruction and out-of-distribution (OOD) extrapolation, while mechanism recovery is assessed on the subset of 161 systems. We evaluate trajectory fidelity across 11 symbolic-discovery methods and assess mechanism recovery for three reaction-based methods. Joint analysis across systems highlights how severely trajectory-based evaluation overestimates true mechanism recovery. Motivated by these findings, we develop KineSelect, a framework that searches candidate reaction topologies under biologically grounded kinetic laws to select optimal mechanisms that balance trajectory fidelity with structural parsimony. Compared with the strongest baseline, KineSelect improves aggregate OOD extrapolation \(R^2\) by 19.2\% and overall reaction F1 score by 14.3\%.

papers.title: Do Machine Learning Ensembles Beat Published Quotas? Target Parameterization, Censored Baselines, and Conformal Intervals Under Admissions Reform
papers.summary: Public admission capacity caps published prior to matriculation are widely used by ministries and institutional analysts as default intake projections in centralized postsecondary clearinghouses. Using an audited 2022 to 2026 Vietnamese undergraduate panel (26,895 program-year records across 309 universities) linked to strictly lagged t-1 occupational vacancy signals, this paper evaluates machine learning, multilevel, and censored econometric estimators against published quotas across 5,385 continuing 2024 programs (five-fold university-grouped cross-validation) and 3,348 matched (2,179 grain-consistent) 2025 programs strictly out of time. Because 62.8% of 2024 programs enroll their exact published quota, unanchored log-growth ensembles degrade accuracy, while the worst 5% generate half of total quota error via unfilled "phantom capacity." Controlled target ablations, including a single-factor test under widened non-binding clipping, show that parameterizing the log fill ratio ln(D_it / S_it) instead of log growth reduces 2024 MAE by 21.5% (14.86 to 11.67), aligns ML with Tobit, Cragg, REML HLM, and capped L1 baselines, and lifts combined tuition and institutional-tier TreeSHAP attribution from 2.5% to 45.8%. Hurdle stacking attains the lowest full-census 2024 MAE (H-Hard 11.29; H-Soft 11.32 vs. 12.35, p = 0.022, clearing 10% not 5% FDR; fold-overlap p = 0.134), whereas continuous QA-Stack outperforms H-Soft on mixed-reporting campuses, Tobit (median) ties H-Soft across both 90% MCS sets, and interior-only Cragg-ML lowers RMSE to 28.1. Under Vietnam's 2025 unified-clearing reform, exact filling falls to 10.4%, H-Soft and capped L1 tie quotas (p = 0.979), and 90% cluster-weighted conformal coverage drops from 89.3% to 74.6%. Across 257 reporting campuses, reconciled 2026 national totals (627,114 to 629,256) lie squarely within 604,533 to 662,044.

papers.title: Proceedings of "Accelerating ALICE background simulations: A WGAN Approach to slow-neutron induced TPC loopers" CHEP 2026, 26/05/2026
papers.summary: The simulation of background processes in high-energy physics can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. To provide the most realistic data description at the ALICE experiment using Monte Carlo simulations, we investigated alternative solutions to generate the products of electromagnetic interactions initiated by slow neutrons in the Time Projection Chamber (TPC). Specifically, electrons and positrons from these processes can spiral repeatedly within the magnetic field in the detector (so-called "loopers") and tracking them via full transport frameworks, such as GEANT4, requires extensive computing resources. A fast simulation framework based on a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) was developed to speed up the simulation process. Our solution is designed to bypass the significant computational cost associated with transporting neutrons to low energies by directly generating the kinematic properties (e.g., momentum, production vertex) of the resulting electron-positron pairs (from neutron capture) and electrons from Compton scattering. The generative model successfully reproduces the complex multidimensional distributions of the background tracks with high fidelity, maintaining agreement with the full GEANT4 simulation. By replacing the full transport of these specific background components with the WGAN inference, a tenfold speedup is achieved, making the simulation of loopers a negligible component of the total processing time. Moreover, the fast simulation framework is modular, allowing for the future inclusion of other background sources, such as nuclear spallation products.
authors: Andreas Morsch for the ALICE Collaboration

papers.title: AlignPre: Skill-Aligned Post-Training for Latent-Free Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
papers.summary: Precipitation nowcasting requires accurate short-term predictions under rapidly evolving spatiotemporal dynamics. Generative diffusion models can produce detailed and competitive radar forecasts by modeling conditional distributions. However, most existing approaches rely on separately trained components, such as deterministic branches or latent compression modules. More fundamentally, distribution matching alone fails to explicitly optimize operational forecast skill. We propose AlignPre, a streamlined pixel-space nowcasting framework that bridges this gap via skill-aligned post-training (SAPT). AlignPre employs an end-to-end flow-matching forecaster with a hierarchical spatiotemporal architecture for distribution matching and direct radar-field synthesis, without latent compression. During post-training, SAPT exploits the analytic structure of forecast verification scores to construct a differentiable objective. By backpropagating gradients of this objective from radar fields to the generator, SAPT turns forecast verification into direct training feedback. Across three real-world benchmarks spanning different forecast horizons, AlignPre consistently surpasses state-of-the-art deterministic and generative baselines in forecast skill, demonstrating that aligning generative modeling with domain-specific verification provides an effective paradigm for meteorological forecasting.

papers.title: Will AI Replace Juniors? How Task Complexity Reduces Automation Risk
papers.summary: How does task complexity shape firms' willingness to substitute entry-level labour with artificial intelligence (AI) tools? We study this question using a pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms in the information economy and manufacturing industry. Managers are randomly assigned to consider a long lasting need for additional capacity involving either well-structured and standardised tasks, or more complex tasks that require professional judgement, contextual knowledge and independent problem-solving. Relative to standardised tasks, complex tasks reduce willingness to use AI rather than hire an entry-level employee by 0.54 points on a five-point scale and increase the importance attached to human oversight by 0.15 points. Further, pre-treatment responses indicate that managers expect the availability of AI applications to reduce hiring of both entry-level employees and experienced workers, but significantly more strongly for entry-level workers.

papers.title: Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries
papers.summary: We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity. We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. However, if one restricts oneself to classical theory, one can argue that the ghosts {\it are} benign (benign classical ghostly system is a system that needs an infinite time to reach a singularity, and it seems to the case both in ordinary and in HD gravity: the cosmic censorship conjecture implies that the singularities are always surrounded by horizons, and it takes an infinite time on the clocks of a distant observer to reach a horizon). Finally, I discuss supersymmetric HD theories: conformal supergravity, where the ghosts are also probably benign, and then an interesting supersymmetric HD gauge theory in 6 dimensions. It involves a dimensionless coupling constant, is renormalizable and rather beautiful. Unfortunately, it is not unitary --- ghosts are not benign there.

papers.title: Exploring the Design Factors of Pixel-space Diffusion
papers.summary: In this paper, we introduce EiT by exploring the key design factors of pixel-space diffusion from three perspectives: model architecture, representation, and frequency domain. Inspired by Denoising Autoencoders (DAE) which perform denoising through a bottleneck, we construct a U-shaped pixel diffusion transformer that performs explicit compression along the channel dimension. In terms of representation, we find that both pixel and latent diffusion transformers exhibit a three-stage representation dynamics across layers and timesteps: denoising/local feature expansion, basis lift-up, and posterior projection. Moreover, earlier denoising and a longer basis lift-up stage are associated with better generation, which EiT naturally achieves through its channel bottleneck and increased network depth. From the frequency perspective, we establish the equivalence between pixel-space and frequency-space diffusion when keeping the network operating in pixel space. On ImageNet $256\times256$ and $512\times512$, EiT consistently outperforms JiT (Just image Transformers) in generation quality. Specifically, our EiT achieves better FID than JiT: 1.61 vs. 1.85 at $256\times256$, and 1.73 vs. 1.99 at $512\times512$. Remarkably, EiT can be seamlessly applied to video pixel diffusion by simply extending the patch size to temporal dimension and outperforms video latent diffusion in FVD evaluated on Kinetics-600 (resolution 256), under comparable total network parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/forever208/EiT

papers.title: Improving Tail-Augmented Speculative Drafting with Hidden State Mixing and Gradient Detach
papers.summary: Multi-token prediction (MTP) modules and EAGLE-style drafters support efficient speculative decoding by reusing target-model hidden states. Their autoregressive use, however, introduces a training-inference mismatch: training supplies sequences of hidden states from the backbone or a single MTP step, whereas inference attends to a target-model prefix followed by a growing tail of recurrently generated MTP states. EAGLE-3's training-time test (TTT) explicitly simulates this behavior during training, at the cost of additional memory and specialized attention masks. We introduce two training-only methods for improving autoregressive drafting. Hidden State Mixing (HSM) samples among backbone and MTP hidden states aligned to the same prediction target, exposing the drafter to mixtures of states from different MTP steps without explicitly simulating inference. Hidden State Gradient Detach (HSGD) is a regularization method that stochastically blocks gradients through hidden state and embedding pathways while preserving the forward computation. Neither method adds inference cost. In joint pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning, HSGD yields the highest acceptance rates at early draft positions, while HSM performs best later in the draft. These acceptance rate trends favor HSM for long-draft-length serving and HSGD for short-draft-length serving. Furthermore, across four Nemotron models and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, HSM-based MTP boosting with a frozen backbone improves mean acceptance length by up to 52.2% over the co-trained MTP. For EAGLE-3 drafters, HSM offers competitive acceptance with TTT, with 48% lower peak reserved training memory in a four-step Qwen3-8B comparison. HSM implementations are publicly available in Megatron-LM and NVIDIA Model Optimizer.

papers.title: Disciplined Anthropomorphism: How to Extend Cognitive Language to Artificial Intelligence
papers.summary: Researchers increasingly describe AI in cognitive terms such as "understanding" and "believing", while critics denounce this as wishful anthropomorphism. Both sides align in taking a subsumptive approach, however: they ask whether AI systems fall under concepts minted for human beings, reporting verdicts as discoveries about those systems when they are largely determined by conceptual frames. Yet the problem AI poses is precisely the problem of how to conceptually frame these systems, and the explosive rise of anthropomorphism is best seen as a response to this problem that needs disciplining rather than discouragement. A disciplined anthropomorphism, I argue, should disentangle the inferential connections bundled up in our cognitive concepts and ask which connections to preserve, sever, or forge for AI. The disciplining then comes, on the one hand, from the human conceptual needs that give point to the drawing of these connections and motivate the concepts' extension in the first place; and, on the other hand, from empirical and especially mechanistic evidence that supports and constrains these connections. By reverse-engineering a concept's point in relation to a particular need before re-engineering it to better serve that point in our dealings with AI, anthropomorphizing extensions can be point-based, transposing the work those concepts do for us while revising the inferential workings through which they do it. Transposing human-tailored conceptions of understanding and belief on the pivot of the underlying conceptual needs gives us just the definitional freedom required to accommodate how AI systems differ from us, yielding conceptions that are not just thinned-out versions of existing ones, but potentially richer and better fitted to the peculiarities of AI.

papers.title: Feature Engineered Reinforcement Learning for S-pair Selection in Buchberger's Algorithm
papers.summary: Selecting the order in which to process S-pairs is a crucial decision in Buchberger's algorithm for computing Groebner bases: this choice can change the cost by orders of magnitude. Recent work has shown that reinforcement learning agents viewing exponent vectors of the polynomials outperform classical heuristics on binomial ideals. We extend this line of work to general polynomial ideals by using statistical features. We introduce a 17-dimensional feature vector to describe a polynomial and use PPO to train policies on five distributions of random ideals. We find that using S-polynomial features significantly outperforms S-pair features on all five distributions. The new policies also outperform the retrained RL baseline on all five distributions, reducing algorithmic work by 41--53\% relative to the degree heuristic on four distributions where learning helps. The additional cost of the feature engineering means that wall-clock cost remains similar to the baseline, but our new approach benefits from easier transfer to unseen distributions.

papers.title: Mathematical modeling of regime-dependent thermal response in multilayer wall assemblies with equal total steady thermal resistance
papers.summary: Steady thermal resistance is a fundamental characteristic of building-envelope assemblies; however, equal steady resistance does not uniquely determine their transient thermal behavior. This study aims to numerically separate the effects of layer order, temperature-dependent thermophysical properties, and redistribution of thermal resistance between bulk and interfacial components in stationarily equivalent multilayer wall assemblies subjected to periodic and finite-pulse thermal loading. A one-dimensional transient heat-conduction model with Robin boundary conditions, finite interfacial thermal resistance, and source-supported temperature-dependent material properties was employed. All compared configurations were constrained to the same total steady thermal resistance at the reference temperature, $R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 3.65315$ m$^2$ K/W. The numerical implementation passed the adopted verification procedure with restrictions. The combined grid/time uncertainty was 0.325 %, below the prescribed 0.5 % acceptance criterion. For the tested pair differing only in layer order, the relative effect was -0.905 % for the periodic decrement factor and +0.566 % for the finite-pulse peak transmission ratio, with effect-to-uncertainty ratios of 79.2 and 88.9, respectively; the opposite signs therefore refer to two distinct regime-specific metrics. The temperature-dependent configuration produced a numerically resolved periodic effect of -2.005 %, whereas the corresponding pulse effect of -0.282 % remained below the adopted numerical-resolution threshold. For a compensated 5-10 % redistribution of bulk thermal resistance to interfacial contacts, the additional dynamic effect was likewise unresolved. The results demonstrate the value of controlled factor separation combined with explicit numerical-uncertainty assessment when evaluating transient thermal behavior.
papers.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Published version of the conference paper presented at the 78th International Conference on Vibroengineering, Lviv, Ukraine, October 2026

papers.title: Defect Correlators from Supergravity: Finding the Missing Contact Terms
papers.summary: We resolve a puzzle in the computation of holographic correlators using supergravity when defects are present. Previous direct supergravity calculations of defect two-point functions were found to differ from bootstrap results by a set of contact contributions. We show that the discrepancy arises from two effects: nonlinear Kaluza-Klein field redefinitions in the bulk, which induce additional quadratic couplings when applied consistently to localized sources, and off-shell terms in mixed bulk--defect vertices, which can collapse internal defect propagators. We demonstrate how these two mechanisms resolve the puzzle in two concrete examples in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, where we consider two-point correlators in the presence of a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson line and on $\mathbb{RP}^4$.

papers.title: Gaussian Process Stochastic Frontiers with Two-Way Fixed Effects
papers.summary: Parametric frontier restrictions and unobserved time heterogeneity can distort efficiency measurement in panel data. This paper develops a Bayesian stochastic frontier model with a Gaussian process prior and unrestricted individual and time effects that may be correlated with inputs. Conditional on inefficiency, orthogonal projection eliminates both sets of fixed effects, yielding a restricted likelihood that retains observation-specific inefficiency. Monte Carlo experiments show competitive performance under correct parametric specification and improved performance when benchmark models impose an incorrect frontier functional form or omit time effects. An application to Spanish dairy farms observed from 1999 to 2010 yields similar average technical efficiency across specifications, but a lower posterior mean of average returns to scale, with greater uncertainty, under the Gaussian process frontier. Models with year effects also yield more stable estimated efficiency profiles than the benchmark with a quadratic trend and time-input interactions. These findings show that conclusions about scale economies and efficiency dynamics depend on both frontier flexibility and the treatment of time heterogeneity.

papers.title: Pseudospin-mediated broadband hypersonic phonon transport beyond localized Berry curvature
papers.summary: Phononic nanostructures offer compact and highly confined control of elastic waves for signal transport, filtering, and quantum transduction. More recently, topological phononic structures have been explored as a route to robust waveguiding around defects and sharp bends, offering a promising basis for scalable and reliable phononic circuitry. However, how robust transport can persist as conventional localized Berry-curvature signatures diminish with increasing structural perturbation remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate bend-resilient hypersonic phonon transport beyond the conventional valley Hall framework. Using an engineered propeller phononic crystal operating at 1.9 GHz, we continuously increase the geometric perturbation to gradually weaken the valley topology while enhancing modal pseudospin character. Strikingly, as the Berry curvature progressively delocalizes from valleys, the complete elastic bandgap broadens to a normalized width of 34% and the interface modes become more strongly confined. Two-port electromechanical measurements on a thin-film lithium niobate-on-SOI platform experimentally confirm broadband interface-mode transport with no measurable bend-induced loss, despite the absence of well-localized valley-topology signatures. Our findings establish modal pseudospin engineering as a powerful design principle for robust acoustic guiding beyond conventional topological constraints, paving the way for broadband hypersonic phononic circuitry for classical and quantum information processing.

papers.title: Quantum Geometric Origin of Néel-Order-Driven Magneto-Optical Response in MnTe
papers.summary: Magneto-optical (MO) responses provide a direct probe of magnetic order, yet resolving compensated antiferromagnetic order remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate in altermagnetic MnTe that the symmetry of the Néel order is imprinted on the MO response through distinct quantum-geometric contributions. Combining first-principles calculations with a Landau symmetry framework, we demonstrate that the quantum metric gives rise to a twofold optical anisotropy, with its diagonal and symmetric off-diagonal components forming an $E_{2g}$ doublet associated with the quadratic Néel-order invariants, providing a characteristic MO Voigt signature of the Néel-vector orientation. In contrast, the Berry curvature generates a complementary threefold Hall response governed by the cubic $A_{2g}$ Néel-order invariant. Although the Hall conductivity and the out-of-plane weak-ferromagnetic moment share the same symmetry and angular dependence, constraining the latter to zero leaves the optical Hall response essentially unchanged demonstrating that the Hall response originates directly from the compensated Néel order rather than the net magnetization. Our results establish quantum geometry as a direct link between Néel order and MO response, revealing distinct twofold and threefold optical signatures of Néel order in altermagnetic MnTe.

papers.title: Exact Error Analysis of Noise-Domain OTFS with Paired Covariance Signaling
papers.summary: Noise-domain orthogonal time frequency space (ND-OTFS) encodes bits through opposite correlations in Gaussian delay--Doppler pairs of equal average energy. This letter derives the exact conditional bit error probability (BEP) of maximum-likelihood detection using generalized covariance eigenvalues and characteristic-function inversion. For scalar channels, we obtain an incomplete-beta expression and its finite-sum Rayleigh average. Partial correlation yields an error floor for a fixed observation count. At unit correlation, the conditional BEP decays with an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exponent equal to the number of pair observations, and common Rayleigh fading yields diversity order one. Simulations validate the analysis and quantify pair-placement effects.

papers.title: Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods for Multiobjective Optimization over Probability Measures via Hilbert-Space Lifting
papers.summary: Many sampling and inference tasks require a single distribution that balances several targets. We formulate this task as multiobjective optimization of Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences over probability measures, in the Pareto sense. The particle method MWGraD (Nguyen et al., 2025) uses explicit Wasserstein gradient steps, and its accelerated version A-MWGraD (Nguyen et al., 2026) lacks discrete-time guarantees. We propose the multiobjective Wasserstein proximal gradient (MWPG), which uses implicit Wasserstein gradient steps, and its accelerated version, multiobjective Wasserstein accelerated proximal gradient (MWAPG), with rigorous discrete-time guarantees. Our key idea is a Hilbert-space lifting: each measure is represented as the pushforward of a fixed base measure by a map in a Hilbert space. The problem then becomes a constrained multiobjective composite problem over transport maps, to which accelerated proximal gradient methods apply. For convex and smooth potentials, we show that MWAPG decreases a Pareto merit function at the rate $\mathcal{O}(1/k^2)$; for $m$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth potentials, the rate is $\mathcal{O}\big((1-\sqrt{m/L})^k\big)$. We also give closed-form Gaussian updates and particle implementations based on input-convex neural networks, which require no score estimation. Experiments on synthetic and real-world dataset show that MWAPG needs far fewer iterations than MWPG and matches or outperforms A-MWGraD in Bayesian multi-task learning.

papers.title: Frustration in system with intercalated and bilayer smectic structure
papers.summary: The dimeric mesogens exhibit an unusual variety of mesophases - nematic and smectic, with distinctly different packing schemes. The relation between molecular and mesophase structure was studied for homologue series of non-symmetric bent dimers CBO6.Om, obtained by serial Pd- and Pt-catalyzed cross-coupling chemical reactions. The shorter homologues of the series form smectics with an intercalated structure, and longer homologues form bilayer smectics with broken up-down symmetry of molecular orientation within the layers, for intermediate homologues frustration leads to a nematic gap. The additional structure complexity arises from the tendency of bent dimers to form twisted structures, in which the azimuthal angle of tilted molecules forms both short- and long-pitch helices. Here we confirm, through resonant X-ray diffraction, that longer homologues form a helical four-layer structure of SmCTB-SH phase, along with a more complex one in which, in addition to the basic four-layer unit, an extra helix is superimposed, SmCTB-DH phase. This additional helix has a periodicity that is strongly temperature-dependent; upon cooling, it changes from 100 nm to 40 nm.

papers.title: A new method of Ecological Inference based on the Cressie--Read power divergence
papers.summary: Ecological inference aims to estimate the bivariate association structure between a pair of variables from the row and column totals of a set of contingency tables. The paper introduces a new approach based on minimizing the Cressie--Read power divergence, applied to the estimation of vote transitions between two elections. It also outlines a Fisher scoring algorithm and derives the asymptotic distribution of the estimator.

papers.title: Toward a quantum resistance standard above liquid nitrogen temperature
papers.summary: Quantum Hall effect (QHE) -- the pioneering demonstration of one-dimensional topologically-protected edge channels -- manifest a transversal resistance quantized solely by two universal constants $e$ and $h$ (the elementary charge and the Planck constant, respectively), referred to as the von Klitzing constant $R_\mathrm{K}=h/e^{2}$. For decades, this has enabled a unique route for realizing quantum Hall resistance (QHR) standard in the Système international d'unitès (SI), yet high precision QHR under relaxed conditions, especially temperature higher than 30 K, has not been possible. Here, we show that interfacial charge-order coupling inbetween CrOCl and monolayer graphene offers enhanced Fermi velocity, creating a robust Landau cyclotron gap. Using a customized direct current comparator (DCC, mounted at room temperature), we obtain relative deviation of the Hall resistance from $R_\mathrm{K}/2$ of (15 $\pm$ 23)\,n$Ω$ $Ω$$^{-1}$ (23 parts per billion of relative uncertainty) at 50 K, with an external magnetic field of 12 T and a dc current of 10 $μ$A. At 100 K, the system exhibits QHR with 2 parts per million of relative uncertainty. Our results therefore suggest a platform toward a next-generation quantum resistance standard that may work at above liquid nitrogen temperature and free of conventional compressor refrigerators.

papers.title: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding
papers.summary: Ad platforms and marketplaces show bidders a bid landscape, the estimated chance of winning at each candidate bid, and increasingly let agents built on reasoning language models choose the bid. We give six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters such landscapes, with win curves from eBay closing prices and from a simulated advertising market (AuctionNet), and score their bids on held-out auctions against an exact calculator. Because the agent is handed the estimates, the lost value can be split by cause. Two failures belong to the models. They pass over the best option even when the values written in their own trace already rank it first, and their wrong answers lean toward the highest bid on the menu. The lean is about the bid's size, not its place in the list, and it survives sampling. At 768 forced tokens on eBay, under pay-your-bid pricing, the wrong answers cost bidders 7-17% of the surplus the calculator's bids earn. Arithmetic errors are rare. Two further losses come from operator choices. A token cap cuts traces short: allowed to stop on their own within 4,096 tokens, five models recover 91-100% of the calculator's lead over a model that does no reasoning. Asking for the answer while the reasoning block is still open misreads it: closing the block first lifts the weakest model from 42% to 84% on eBay and from 24% to 81% on AuctionNet. Finally, an audit that flags bids disagreeing with the trace's own numbers, and overrides them with the calculator's bid, raises the share of the calculator's lead recovered at 768 forced tokens from 42-85% to 84-100% on eBay under nested cross-validation, and the same reader settings transfer from eBay to AuctionNet.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 2 figures, 23 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/DataismLab/bid-reasoning

papers.title: A Path Integral Method with Far-Field Expansion for Open Quantum Dynamics
papers.summary: We establish a connection between the quasi-adiabatic propagator path integral (QuAPI) method and fast resummation of Dyson series (FRODS). Building on this connection, we introduce a path integral method with far-field expansion (PIFFE) for quantum systems coupled linearly to a thermal Gaussian bath. PIFFE combines QuAPI with a Taylor expansion of the far-field bath influence, keeping interactions within $r$ time steps in exponential form. The scheme has error $O(Δt^2)$ at fixed final time and is free of stochastic or tensor-compression errors. Spin-boson tests show that PIFFE gives results much closer to QuAPI than FRODS does, even for small $r$, while requiring substantially less storage than QuAPI. This allows much longer bath memory lengths and simulations of multilevel systems. Truncating the bath memory and limiting the total auxiliary degree further reduce storage and computational costs.

papers.title: Prethermalization of entanglement entropy in the mixed-field Ising model
papers.summary: We study how weak integrability breaking affects the dynamics of the half-chain entanglement entropy of random product states in the mixed-field Ising model. The associated Hamiltonian depends on two parameters $g$ and $h$ determining the sizes of the longitudinal and transverse fields and has two integrable limits: the classical Ising chain $(h=0)$ and the transverse-field Ising model $(g=0)$. Weak perturbations of these limits give rise to the short-range network (SRN) and long-range network (LRN) regimes, respectively. We characterize the departure from integrable dynamics and the emergence of intermediate entanglement plateaus by melting times $T_M$ at prescribed entropy thresholds and analyze their dependence on the perturbation strength. For the SRN parameters examined away from $g=2$, we find $T_M\propto h^{-2}$ over the thresholds tested. At $g=2$, the relaxation splits into two stages: an initial departure from the integrable plateau with $T_M\propto h^{-1}$, followed by the melting of a well-defined intermediate prethermal plateau with $T_{M_2}\propto h^{-2}$. In the LRN regime, by contrast, the inverse of $T_M$ scales with exponents of $g$ close to either one or two, depending on the parameter values, the system size, and the entropy threshold, and no well-defined prethermal plateaus are observed. Our analysis distinguishes the melting of integrable dynamics from the subsequent decay of a prethermal plateau, which is observed in the SRN regime.

papers.title: Gradient Optical Diffraction Tomography Using Deep Learning-Assisted Amplitude Estimation
papers.summary: Gradient Optical Diffraction Tomography (GODT) enables the non-invasive reconstruction of a spatial derivative of the 3D sample's refractive index distribution, providing enhanced sensitivity to subtle refractive index variations through gradient-based contrast. Implemented using lateral shearing interferometry (LSI), GODT benefits from a common-path architecture that provides environmental stability and high signal-to-noise ratio measurements. Unlike conventional optical diffraction tomography (ODT), which requires numerical integration of LSI-derived phase gradients to recover the object phase, GODT enables direct tomographic reconstruction from the LSI data. Notably, GODT requires derivatives of both the phase and amplitude of the object fields as input. While the phase derivative can be readily extracted from LSI data, the amplitude gradient cannot be directly retrieved. Thus, in the original GODT formulation, the amplitude gradient was assumed to be negligible, limiting the accuracy of the resulting 3D reconstruction. In this work, we introduce amplitude-informed GODT (AI-GODT), which employs physics-informed supervised deep learning to estimate the missing amplitude gradient based on accessible LSI data, specifically the fringe modulation. The proposed approach, applying a ResNet architecture and training on computer-generated data, is validated through numerical simulation and experimental measurements of both a well-characterized test object and primary neuronal cell culture, demonstrating the network's ability to generalize to diverse samples. We show that incorporation of the recovered amplitude gradient into the GODT reconstruction pipeline improves the 3D reconstruction quality, especially in its out-of-focus regions. The software and datasets are openly available to facilitate reproducibility and further development.

papers.title: Dopamine: A Cartesian grid large-eddy-simulation framework for coastal ocean modelling of free-surface waves
papers.summary: We present a Cartesian staggered-grid large-eddy simulation framework for modelling coastal ocean waves using the Dopamine solver. The framework combines a geometric volume-of-fluid method for simulating free-surface wave evolution with one-way-coupled Lagrangian point-particle tracking for heavy and buoyant particles. A ghost-cell immersed-boundary method represents stationary solid boundaries, including the seabed and coastal obstacles, and their interaction with free-surface waves. The framework includes the Vreman and anisotropic minimum-dissipation (AMD) sub-grid-scale models for simulating near-wall turbulence. Comparisons with analytical solutions and established experimental and numerical benchmarks illustrate the framework's ability to reproduce wave dynamics and particle motion. The results provide promising insights into the framework's capabilities for coastal ocean modelling applications focused on investigating small-scale turbulent physics using a low-numerical-dissipation approach. The solver runs on multi-CPU architectures, with two-fluid strong- and weak-scaling efficiencies at 512 ranks relative to 64 ranks of up to 77% and 73%, respectively, and a single-GPGPU build has been verified against the CPU solver.

papers.title: Design-based causal inference for ROC curves
papers.summary: In randomized experiments, causal inference traditionally focuses on the average treatment effect, yet comparing the treatment and control potential outcome distributions is often of interest. Under complete randomization, we adopt a design-based framework without imposing an outcome model to study the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, which measures the proportion of treated outcomes exceeding each upper quantile of the control distribution. We propose an estimator that depends only on pooled outcome ranks, establish its asymptotic normality, and construct conservative variance estimators and confidence intervals. We also develop covariate adjustment directly for the ROC estimator, preserving the target estimand while achieving an asymptotic variance no larger than that of the unadjusted estimator. We further construct simultaneous confidence bands over an interior range of quantile levels and extend pointwise inference to the extreme upper tail of the control distribution, with both extensions accommodating covariate adjustment. Simulation studies and an application to a large-scale online learning experiment illustrate the proposed methods.

papers.title: CARE-WM: Same-Horizon Self-Conditioning with Constraint-Adaptive Regularization for Latent World Models
papers.summary: Planning with latent world models requires both accurate multi-step predictions and latent distances that reflect physical proximity to the goal. However, models are typically trained on ground-truth observations but must rely on their own imaginations during planning, while closer latent distances do not necessarily correspond to better task outcomes. Existing methods resort to auxiliary training objectives or additional task-cost readouts, which respectively incur extra training overhead or leave the latent geometry itself misaligned with task cost. We introduce CARE-WM, a drop-in training method that meets both requirements without additional supervision, a separate cost model, or any change to LeWM's architecture and Euclidean-cost planner. CARE-WM trains the predictor on its own predictions and adaptively calibrates the strength of latent regularization. With a single hyperparameter configuration, CARE-WM improves mean planning success over LeWM across all evaluated continuous-control tasks and matches or exceeds the best results of other LeWM-family methods on most tasks. Further analyses show lower open-loop latent prediction error and closer agreement between latent-cost rankings and physical task costs.

papers.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
papers.summary: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. We trace these failures to the asymmetry between reading and modification directions during erasure, which yields non-normal erase operators whose directional gains accumulate across tokens, triggering exponential state growth even without new writes. To resolve this, we propose \model{}, employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility. Theoretically, we establish an $O(\sqrt{T})$ upper bound on recurrent state growth while retaining chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that \model{} achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting and average accuracy across nine downstream tasks by 0.62 points in the hybrid setting.

papers.title: UNIONS and Euclid: Calibrating point source-galaxy separation for ground-based surveys
papers.summary: Efficient separation of unresolved point sources from extended objects (star-galaxy separation) is essential for deep wide-field imaging surveys, particularly at faint magnitudes where morphological differences become subtle. We assess two morphology-based classification methods applied to single-band, ground-based imaging from the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS), using Euclid observations as a high-fidelity reference to evaluate their performance and to train one of the methods. We analysed 8 deg$^2$ of overlapping UNIONS $r$-band and Euclid $I_E$ data, comprising more than $7\times10^{5}$ sources. The Euclid data enable robust morphological labelling down to $I_E\simeq 26$, which we used to train and validate two classification approaches applied to UNIONS alone: a curve-of-growth method and a supervised neural-network classifier, both based on aperture photometry and image-quality information. The curve-of-growth method yields an almost perfectly complete point-source sample ($>95\%$), but its purity decreases rapidly at $r \simeq 22.5$. The neural-network approach significantly improves the purity at the faint end, maintaining $\geq 80\%$ purity down to $r \simeq 24$, while the completeness decreases to almost $50\%$ at similar depths. In both cases, performance strongly depends on the image quality of the ground-based data. This work shows how Euclid data can be used to develop, calibrate, and validate star-galaxy separation methods for ground-based surveys, useful in regions not covered by Euclid. Both methods have already been applied to UNIONS data and are readily applicable to future surveys such as LSST, offering flexible solutions depending on whether completeness or purity is prioritised.
papers.comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. Some material is available online on https://github.com/GFThomas/StarGal_ground_Euclid

papers.title: Nonparametric predictive inference for interval-censored data: M-functions anchored to the self-consistent estimator
papers.summary: Nonparametric predictive inference specifies the distribution of a future observation through M-functions, which are basic probability assignments on intervals. Here such a specification is proposed for data censored on the left, on the right or within intervals of arbitrary width. It is the union of two M-functions. The first rests on a post-data assumption under which each censored observation divides its predictive mass equally amongst the observations with regions inside its own, and it reproduces the right-censored theory exactly. The second combines the Turnbull estimator with one unconstrained unit of predictive mass. The resulting survival bounds contain the Turnbull estimator, lie inside the bounds from all completions of the data and need no enumeration. In simulated inspection schemes they were calibrated for fixed events and for the rank of a further observation, while the second member alone was not. Equal weights on all orderings allowed by the data give the first member whenever the regions are nested or disjoint. The method is compared with the Turnbull estimator on two interval-censored studies.
papers.comment: 18 pages, with 13 pages of supplementary material

papers.title: Reliable User Simulation in Complex Multi-Step Workflows
papers.summary: LLM-based user simulators are increasingly used to evaluate conversational assistants. Yet, these simulators can drift from their assigned goals or fail to exhaustively explore all specified options, causing evaluation errors incorrectly attributed to the assistant. Prior work has examined goal alignment in single-task settings, but many practical scenarios require simulators to execute multi-step workflows with sequential tasks, fallback logic, and cross-task dependencies, where simulator fidelity has not been measured. To close this gap, we introduce a benchmark of 500 workflows represented using the Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) abstraction. Our experiments reveal that the simulator's fidelity degrades sharply with workflow complexity, and that goal drift accounts for the majority of failures. Fidelity also depends on the assistant's response style, with the same simulator scoring substantially better or worse across styles. To address this, we propose ReUST (Reasoning + User State Tracking), a simple prompting strategy to maintain state information across dialogue turns. ReUST improves goal success rate by more than 12 points for mid-sized and large models, and reduces simulator sensitivity to the assistant's response style.

papers.title: Too Smart for Its Own Good? Cognitive Fidelity and Competence Leakage in LLM Simulations of Young Learners
papers.summary: LLM-based interactive learner simulators are increasingly used in educational applications, including teacher training and tutoring system development. A critical requirement for those simulations is cognitive fidelity: the simulated learner should maintain the assigned knowledge, misconceptions, and reasoning procedures throughout interaction. However, LLMs may express knowledge or problem-solving skills beyond the assigned learner's cognitive status, a phenomenon we refer to as competence leakage. In this exploratory study, we examine 3,339 simulated learner utterances from 130 teacher-learner simulator transcripts across three learning scenarios and identify over-competence as a prominent direction of cognitive-profile misalignment during interaction. We then investigate the recurrence of previously observed competence leakage cases under four matched-trigger evaluation protocols, ranging from isolated questioning to multi-turn interactions, across five model configurations. Overall, we observe higher violation recurrence under multi-turn protocols than under isolated question answering. More capable models generally show lower recurrence, whereas increased reasoning effort does not consistently improve cognitive fidelity and is even associated with slightly higher recurrence under multi-turn protocols in our matched-model comparison. These findings provide exploratory evidence of competence leakage phenomena in interactive learner simulation and suggest that single-turn question-answering type of evaluations alone may be insufficient, motivating the development of more systematic and reliable multi-turn protocols for evaluating cognitive fidelity in learner simulation.

papers.title: Minimal input dimension for superactivation of one-shot zero-error quantum capacity
papers.summary: The one-shot zero-error quantum capacity $\overline{Q}_0$ is studied within the framework of noncommutative graphs of quantum channels. The additivity of $\overline{Q}_0$ is proved for an arbitrary finite collection of channels with two-dimensional input spaces. An explicit pair of noncommutative graphs $S,T\subset M_3$ exhibiting superactivation of the one-shot zero-error quantum capacity is also constructed. Together, these results establish that the minimum input dimension for such superactivation is $3$.

papers.title: Asymptotically Efficient Finite Impulse Response System Identification without Noise Knowledge
papers.summary: Efficient identification of finite impulse response systems under unknown or heavy-tailed noise remains a challenge in system identification. Classical estimators, including least squares (LS) and robust alternatives like least absolute deviations (LAD), are often sensitive to outliers or statistically inefficient when noise characteristics deviate from their underlying assumptions. To address this, we propose a novel class of adaptive estimators that achieves asymptotic efficiency without requiring prior knowledge of the noise distribution. Our approach leverages kernel density estimation to construct two nonparametric maximum likelihood-type estimators: the estimated maximum likelihood estimator (eMLE) and the estimated profiled MLE (epMLE). These estimators approximate the likelihood using residuals from consistent initial estimates, avoiding parametric assumptions on the noise. We establish theoretical guarantees showing that, under mild regularity conditions, both eMLE and epMLE are consistent, asymptotically normal, and attain the Cramér--Rao lower bound, thereby achieving asymptotic efficiency. Additionally, we develop computationally efficient one-step Newton--Raphson algorithms that implement these estimators without sacrificing asymptotic efficiency. Extensive simulations across various noise distributions confirm that the proposed methods outperform classical LS and LAD estimators in both robustness and accuracy, often matching oracle MLE performance.

papers.title: On the level lines of bilayer potentials with a finite number of harmonics
papers.summary: We consider ``bilayer'' potentials formed by the superposition of two periodic potentials in a plane. We assume that both potentials share the same rotational symmetry and employ an approximation involving a finite number of harmonics in their Fourier expansions. An analysis of the level lines of the resulting quasiperiodic potential (a problem posed by S.P. Novikov) near the percolation threshold makes it possible to describe the behavior of large-scale closed level lines in this limit. The results presented here can also be applied to broader classes of bilayer potentials that possess ``good'' analytical properties.

papers.title: Towards Quark-Gluon Correlations in Pion from the Dyson-Schwinger Equations
papers.summary: Twist-3 distributions encode quark-gluon correlations, and the pion's chiral-odd $e(x)$ is the simplest of them. QCD fixes its lowest moments exactly, yet the only rainbow-ladder (RL) calculation of $e(x)$ omitted the Wilson line and violated the equation-of-motion (EOM) sum rule for the first moment. We show that the discrepancy is not a failure of RL but of the omitted link: at first order in the coupling, the link contributes three classes of planar diagrams that cancel the EOM violation class by class, so the sum rule is restored exactly in RL. The resulting zeroth and first moments are complete RL results. The genuine twist-3 component changes sign near $x=0.45$, and the Wilson line more than doubles its magnitude in the negative region. This identifies the Wilson line as the missing ingredient in the RL description of $e(x)$ and sets the stage for a full resummation of the $gA$ expansion.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Privacy-Preserving Hypothesis Testing via Entanglement-Assisted Classical Communication
papers.summary: Quantum mechanisms satisfying quantum local differential privacy (QLDP) have been shown to achieve a quantum advantage over classical local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms in certain hypothesis-testing problems. While previous demonstrations have considered the transmission of quantum states from users to a server, we investigate whether this advantage can persist under entanglement-assisted classical communication (EACC), where users and the server share entanglement in advance and communicate only classical messages. We formulate an EACC-based hypothesis-testing framework and introduce measurement local differential privacy (MLDP) to protect private inputs against arbitrary shared quantum states and server-side measurements. We establish that QLDP classical-to-quantum channels admit MLDP-compliant EACC simulations and that, in the high-privacy regime, certain optimal QLDP mechanisms can be realized with one-bit classical communication, albeit using high-dimensional entanglement. We then demonstrate that a strict quantum advantage persists even when the pre-shared entanglement is restricted to a single qubit pair and each user communicates only one classical bit. Using EACC protocols based on the geometry of qubit measurements, we establish this advantage for both asymmetric and symmetric hypothesis testing and every input alphabet of size $v \geq 3$ in the high-privacy limit. The ratio of the achieved error exponent to the optimal one under the LDP constraint is at least $5/4$ for all such alphabets and approaches $3/2$ as $v$ grows. These results demonstrate that quantum advantage in locally private hypothesis testing can persist under simultaneous constraints on entanglement dimension and classical communication.

papers.title: Kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
papers.summary: Investigating black hole physics in semi-classical gravitational theory is an interesting and important direction. When the backreaction of the conformal anomaly-induced effective stress-energy tensor is taken into account, the black hole spacetime can be largely altered which changes many properties of the black hole. In this work, rather than restricting our attention to the type-A anomaly, we incorporate the type-B anomaly and investigate how it modifies the spacetime structure obtained when only the type-A anomaly is considered. We find that for a specific relation between the central charges and the cosmological constant, the semiclassical Einstein equations can be solved analytically, yielding a metric that takes the exact form of the Kiselev black hole. After deriving the solution, we further discuss the properties of this new black hole solutions. Our work serves as an essential stepping stone for studying black hole geometries under the full conformal anomaly.

papers.title: JHealthBench-L: Clinician-Reviewed Localization of HealthBench for Rubric-Based Medical LLM Evaluation in Japan
papers.summary: Rubric-based benchmarks such as HealthBench evaluate large language models (LLMs) on open-ended health consultations using case-specific physician criteria, many of which presuppose the healthcare institutions, medications, and care pathways of their source region. Under machine translation alone, these regional assumptions remain in the rubric, leaving responses appropriate in Japan uncredited or falsely penalized under foreign clinical rules. To adapt established clinical evaluation perspectives to Japan without authoring rubrics from scratch, we construct JHealthBench-L (79 patient-facing consultations, 1,022 criteria) through source-cited LLM drafting, single-specialist selection and revision, independent dual-physician review, and meta-review. Specialists rewrote only 4.4% of criteria from scratch, and independent reviewers approved 93.6% of Stage-2 criteria without issue. Comparing JHealthBench-L with a machine-translated baseline across 18 LLMs reveals that translation-only evaluation preserves coarse model rankings ($τ= 0.817$, mean shift +0.027) yet flips verdicts on 17.7% of modified criteria (vs. 7.3% re-grading noise) and reduces false penalties on Japan-adapted negative criteria by 7.1 percentage points, masking item-level clinical mismeasurement behind stable leaderboards. Axis-level and paired analyses further show that context awareness and Japan-specific clinical criteria remain primary bottlenecks, whereas Japanese continual pretraining and reasoning post-training substantially improve locally grounded performance. Datasets, physician revision logs, and evaluation code are available at https://github.com/horshohei/JHealthBench-L.

papers.title: Evaluating Ukrainian Grammatical Competence in Language Models: Probability Versus Prompting
papers.summary: Organisations deploying large language models in Ukrainian-language information systems need to know whether a model produces normative Ukrainian. This paper establishes a protocol for measuring that reliably and applies it to 19 models. The instrument is a released set of 1,444 Ukrainian minimal pairs covering the vocative case, numeral-noun and adjective agreement, verb government and calques from russian, with subject-verb agreement as a control; a quarter of the set was checked against the answer key in two independent native-speaker ratings, which agreed at Cohen's $κ$ = 0.963. Every pair is scored twice: by comparing the probabilities a model assigns to the two sentences, and by asking the model directly, with the sentences presented in both orders so that answer-position effects are measured instead of being absorbed into the score. Three results follow. Order consistency (the share of pairs answered identically when the sentences are exchanged) falls below 0.05 for ten of the nineteen models, and what separates the usable models is instruction tuning, not scale. The vocative case is systematically inverted: 0.153 accuracy against 0.951 on the control, with models preferring the non-normative nominative form of address. Ukrainian adaptation substantially reduces this deficit, measured against the exact checkpoints two adapted models were trained from.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 3 figures. Presented at CITI-2026: 4th International Conference on Computer Information Technologies in Industry 4.0 (Ternopil, Ukraine, November 4-6, 2026); to appear in CEUR Workshop Proceedings. Data and code: https://github.com/DmytroBabarytskyi/ukrainian-minimal-pairs

papers.title: Residual Cross-Model Narrative Convergence under Shared Prompts: Auditing Prompt Controls and Narrative Measurement
papers.summary: Stories created by LLMs based on the same prompts can be narratively similar to one another. This similarity may reflect constraints imposed by the prompts as well as the models' writing tendencies. The current research analyzes 51,240 stories created by five models in the StoryScope corpus based on 10,248 common prompts. It uses 213 narrative features in seven dimensions to compare cross-model distances between stories generated from the same prompts with distances between stories generated from different but semantically matched prompts. To assess the relationship between narrative features and prompt content, a semantic relevance mask was evaluated against 420 author-annotated prompt-feature judgments (F1 = .813; near-threshold accuracy = .621). The equally weighted mean Residual Convergence Index (RCI) was .409 without masking and .406 with masking. These findings indicate measurable cross-model narrative convergence relative to a semantically matched-prompt baseline, with little change following semantic relevance masking.

papers.title: Non-perturbative charm production from color ropes in relativistic heavy ion collisions
papers.summary: We present results on charm production in nucleus-nucleus reactions in the energy range $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5$-$20$ GeV, obtained with the SMASH transport approach extended to include color rope formation. We show that string fusion may provide a substantial additional non-perturbative source of charm production. This may help to explain the apparent charm enhancement (above the pQCD expectations) at low transverse momenta. Our predicted neutral $D$-meson yields are consistent with current experimental constraints and may provide valuable insights for upcoming data by the NA61/SHINE collaboration.

papers.title: Determining the kaon distribution amplitudes by fitting the $D\to K$ transition form factor to investigate the equivalence of two chiral LCSR frameworks
papers.summary: In this work, we fit the $D\to K$ vector transition form factor (TFF) to the BESIII experimental data using a Monte Carlo (MC) method. We also calculate the TFF using QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSRs) with left-and right-handed chiral currents. For the TFF derived using the right-handed chiral current, the key input is the kaon twist-2 distribution amplitude (DA), for which we consider three models: the power-law parametrization ($\mathrm{R1}$), the truncated Gegenbauer expansion ($\mathrm{R2}$), and the light-cone harmonic oscillator (LCHO) model ($\mathrm{R3}$). The parameters of these models are determined by fitting the corresponding TFF predictions to the MC-fit results. For the TFF derived using the left-handed chiral current, the dominant input is the kaon twist-3 DA ($\mathrm{L4}$), which is constructed within the LCHO framework. Its parameters are determined from theoretical constraints rather than from the fit. In the large-recoil region, the resulting TFF are $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R1}}=0.7381^{+0.0180}_{-0.0194}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R2}}=0.7320^{+0.0178}_{-0.0192}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R3}}=0.7324^{+0.0180}_{-0.0191}$, and $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{L4}}=0.7343^{+0.0459}_{-0.0573}$. We then calculate the decay widths and branching fractions of the semileptonic decays $D\to K eν_e$ and extract the CKM matrix element $|V_{cs}|$. Finally, we predict the two important ratios, $\mathcal{R}_{π^-/K^-}^{e}$ and $\mathcal{R}_{π^0/K^0}^{e}$. All the obtained results are consistent with existing experimental measurements and theoretical predictions.

papers.title: Discrete truncated Wigner approximation of the quantum phase transition in the transverse-field Ising model
papers.summary: The discrete truncated Wigner approximation (DTWA) has been a workhorse for large-scale spin dynamics, but whether it captures dynamics across a quantum phase transition has not been tested systematically. In this work, we use the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) to study the quantum phase transition with DTWA from one to three dimensions and with all-to-all connectivity, using slow linear ramps and fast ramps. We find that DTWA cannot capture the dynamics on the one-dimensional chain, and that its behavior is consistent with classical thermalization, in which its classical spins relax toward a thermal state at a finite effective temperature that does not vanish for slow ramps, while a one-dimensional chain cannot order at any finite temperature. For square and cubic lattices, in contrast to the chain, DTWA builds order, and the order sets in close to the quantum critical point found by quantum Monte Carlo (QMC). However, its correlations do not grow with the Kibble-Zurek exponents, so DTWA captures the onset of order but not the universal dynamics of the transition. For all-to-all coupling, DTWA follows the exact growth of the order parameter along the entire ramp. Our results suggest that DTWA becomes more reliable as each spin interacts with more partners, and that beyond one dimension it can indicate where a quantum phase transition lies but cannot capture its critical scaling.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables. Submission to SciPost. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24526315

papers.title: Wannier-Based Low-Energy Electronic Structure Analysis of $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$
papers.summary: The low-energy electronic structures of $λ$-(BETS)$_2$GaCl$_4$ and $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$ were investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and maximally localized Wannier functions (MLWFs). For $λ$-(STF)$_2$GaCl$_4$, DFT-selected and directly XRD-refined structural models were compared before and after fixed-lattice relaxation. Their initially different near-Fermi-level electronic structures become similar after relaxation. Relative to BETS, relaxed STF has a narrower frontier bandwidth while retaining a substantial dimerization energy scale. Two MLWFs were constructed for each selected unrelaxed structure to represent the upper frontier bands, with total spreads of 36.708 Å$^2$ for BETS and 37.578 Å$^2$ for STF. The Wannier-derived transfer integrals show a pronounced reduction of $t_{d1}$ from 51 meV in BETS to 6.5 meV in STF, indicating selective modification of the low-energy electronic connectivity.
papers.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in JPS Conference Proceedings (SCES2026)

papers.title: Rotation curves of dwarf galaxies and dark matter as a condensate of $q$-deformed bosons: reconstruction and fits of the deformation profile
papers.summary: Dark-matter-dominated dwarf galaxies are a sensitive testing ground for models in which dark matter is a self-interacting Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). In the Thomas-Fermi limit the standard BEC halo has the density profile $ρ\propto\sin(kr)/(kr)$, so that the shape of its rotation curve is fixed up to two scale parameters. Here we consider a condensate of $q$-deformed bosons. We show that, in the Thomas-Fermi limit, the deformation enters the structure of the halo only through the chemical potential of the condensate; consequently, a spatially uniform deformation parameter leaves the standard BEC profile unchanged. In every galaxy $χ$ is depressed in the inner region, $kr\lesssim1$, relative to the outer halo, where it is approximately constant in most cases: the standard condensate describes the outer halo, while the core requires a weaker deformation, i.e., $q$ closer to unity. The profiles share this qualitative shape, but neither the depth nor the width of the depression is universal. Modelling the depression by a Gaussian, with two additional parameters, we fit the rotation curves with rms residuals of $0.6$--$2.6$~km\,s$^{-1}$, against $1.6$--$8.5$~km\,s$^{-1}$ for the standard condensate. According to the Bayesian information criterion, the deformed condensate is preferred over the standard condensate, the Navarro-Frenk-White profile, and the Burkert profile in four galaxies, is indistinguishable from the best of them in two, and is disfavoured in two. We discuss the limitations of these results, in particular the absence of error bars in the data, the neglect of baryons, and the phenomenological status of a position-dependent deformation.

papers.title: Milk-removal feedback shapes lactation sustainability and daily output in a model of human lactation
papers.summary: Milk production during lactation is dynamically regulated by milk removal, yet quantitative models linking feeding or pumping schedules to subsequent production remain scarce. We develop a minimal model describing milk accumulation and production between removal sessions, and the stimulation of subsequent production through milk removal. We compare different assumptions about how stimulation depends on the amount of milk removed or the duration of removal, and consider two removal protocols: prescribing either the removed amount or the removal duration. When stimulation depends on the removed amount, declining production can reduce subsequent stimulation and reinforce the decline. This leads to a critical wait interval beyond which no repeated constant schedule can sustain lactation. If stimulation is inefficient for small removal amounts but more efficient at intermediate amounts, the model can exhibit bistability: depending on the initial conditions, milk production either persists or ceases. In contrast, duration-dependent stimulation does not permit a zero-production state under continued removal, but can generate non-constant long-term dynamics under certain conditions. We further show that maximizing milk removal per session need not maximize daily output, because increased removal competes with session frequency. The framework provides a basis for testing alternative feedback hypotheses against longitudinal data and for optimizing feeding and pumping schedules.
papers.comment: 65 pages (44 main + 21 appendix), 13 figures, 1 Supplementary html file

papers.title: An Electromagnetic Ergoregion Limits the Reconnection-Driven Penrose Process
papers.summary: Magnetic reconnection taps black-hole rotational energy via negative-energy ejecta, but field geometry itself can forbid such ejection inside the spacetime ergoregion. We identify a covariant electromagnetic (EM) ergoregion for general degenerate, magnetically dominated fields in stationary spacetimes. Outside the EM ergoregion, even ultrarelativistic field-guided ejecta cannot attain negative Killing energy. For Alfvénic reconnection outflows, the magnetization threshold scales inversely with the transverse distance to the EM ergosurface. The mass-loaded Kerr model places the EM ergosurface at about 75% of the radial interval from the horizon to the spacetime ergosurface, close to the time-averaged boundary inferred from a dynamical simulation. Together, these results show that field geometry determines where negative-energy ejection is possible, while magnetization sets the threshold for realizing it.

papers.title: Formation of Electron Velocity Distribution Functions at low-\{beta} Quasi-Perpendicular Shocks From Physical-Mass-Ratio PIC Simulations
papers.summary: At low-\{beta} quasi-perpendicular shocks, the origins of upstream field-aligned electron beams and downstream flat-top distributions remain unresolved. Using 2D fully kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations at the physical ion-to-electron mass ratio (mi/me = 1836), we found that the shock transition region is dominated by electromagnetic whistler-mode turbulence driven by the modified two-stream instability (MTSI) of reflected ions, not by the electrostatic instabilities as suggested by some previous studies using a reduced mass ratio. Beams in the upstream are produced mainly by shock-drift acceleration (SDA) at the ramp, whereas we attribute the downstream flat-top distributions to nonuniform acceleration by the parallel electric field. Electrons experience different field strengths, polarities, and interaction durations along their trajectories, leading to a spread of parallel velocity changes that broadens and flattens the distribution. These results highlight the importance of using the physical mass ratio in exploring the electron dynamics of low-\{beta} shocks.
papers.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal

papers.title: Exploring Physical Mechanisms Underlying the Emergence of Collective Order
papers.summary: Emergence of collective order from disordered constituents is a hallmark of active matter, and the Vicsek model (VM) serves as a paradigmatic system for its study. However, whether density-induced emergence in the VM differs between angular (intrinsic) and vectorial (extrinsic) noise, and what mechanisms govern the transitions, remain largely unexplored. Remarkably, we uncover that collective order emerges from a disordered state in a continuous-like manner under intrinsic noise but abruptly under extrinsic noise. Combining nonequilibrium landscape-flux theory with a coarse-grained mapping method, we show that the landscape evolves continuously from a single basin to two and back to one under intrinsic noise, but the two-basin landscape appears abruptly under extrinsic noise across the critical transition to flocking. The counterclockwise nonequilibrium flux sustains global circular motion, providing the driving force for reshaping the landscape. The mean flux and entropy production rate change steeply near the emergence threshold and exhibit pronounced peaks within the coexistence region, identifying them as the dynamical and thermodynamic origins of emergence. Our findings reveal a distinct abrupt emergence under extrinsic noise and offer deeper mechanistic insight, practical applications (e.g., locating phase boundaries and distinguishing transition types), and extensibility to other nonequilibrium collective systems.
papers.comment: 19 pages, 11 figures (7 pages, 4 figures for main text; 12 pages, 7 figures for Supplemental Material)

papers.title: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states
papers.summary: We propose a unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar (QMBS) states in the spin-1 {\it XY}, domain-wall-conserving, and Onsager scar models. Model-dependent isometries map the exact scar states to Dicke states and the target asymptotic QMBS states to gapless magnon excitations of the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain. Exact QMBS states are prepared by applying the inverse isometries to Dicke states. For asymptotic QMBS states, block encoding first prepares the magnon excitations from Dicke states to a prescribed fidelity, after which the inverse isometries map the prepared states back to the physical chains. At fixed target fidelity, the block-encoding success probability has a positive lower bound independent of system size and scar index, implying that a constant number of amplitude amplification rounds suffices. Our algorithm enables systematic studies of nonergodic dynamics on programmable quantum simulators.
papers.comment: main: 9 pages, 2 figures, 1 table, supplemental material: 21 pages, 13 figures, 2 tables

papers.title: Certified Outage Bounds for RIS-Assisted NOMA with Source-Side Thermal Energy Harvesting
papers.summary: Gaussian useful-gain and mean-interference approximations can cause opposite power-sizing errors in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). We extend a source-side thermal energy harvesting model with Poisson interference and certify two-sided outage bounds. In a tested environment, the combined required signal-to-noise ratio error has opposite signs at 20 and 24 elements per user. Under another power convention, mean or moment-matched Gamma-distributed interference can predict false feasibility with exact useful gain. In the Gamma case, the Gaussian gain approximation can mask this false feasibility. Propagated Chernoff bounds give sufficient designs. Results concern the specified model and tested regimes.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications Letters. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24450534

papers.title: MolGPAO: Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree with Speculative Decoding and Sub-Millisecond Seam Healing for 3D Molecules
papers.summary: Autoregressive generation over adaptive 3D octrees (Uni-3DAR) offers an intrinsic $O(N \log N)$ sparsity advantage over dense $O(N^2)$ equivariant diffusion and flow models on large drug-like molecules, yet lags in geometric equilibrium, closed-shell valence stability, and property fidelity due to Morton-seam coordinate jumps, leaf-heavy compute with root-count trapping, and target-shortcut collapse in internal critics. We introduce MolGPAO (Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree), a standalone 3D octree architecture and single-output speculative tree-decoding engine using zero external surrogates, zero reinforcement learning, and zero inference-time MLIP relaxation. MolGPAO unifies: (1) non-trapping 6-D ScaleFreeBudgetEmbedding with L5-to-L1 covalent packing priors; (2) a FlashAttention-2 pause-and-gather speculative octree funnel ($m_{s1} \to m_{s2} \to 1$, $M_{\mathrm{out}} = 1$); (3) an anti-shortcut ground-truth TwoStageOctreeProcessCritic with 64-RBF covalent edge gating and $SO(3)$-invariant 12-channel multipole norms (blind QM9 $r = 0.9867$--$0.9989$); (4) a $<0.5$ ms 4-layer $SE(3)$ PostTreeGraphRefiner for Morton-seam healing, expected-XYZ bonded supervision, selective CFG, and zero-heavy-displacement valence reconciliation; and (5) bubble-free stride-2 GPU leaf decoding. Across GEOM-Drugs (0.49 GPU-h), disjoint 50k/50k QM9 (0.43 GPU-h), and PBE0/def2-TZVP-verified OE62 (0.56 GPU-h), MolGPAO lifts drug-scale valid-connected yield 6.78x (12.7% to 86.2%, 99.83% atom stability), runs 7.3x faster (or 1.65x faster at 2.0x yield) than 100-step FlowMol at $N=100$, beats 156 GPU-h PropMolFlow on QM9 HOMO (-12.7%) and dipole (-21.0%) at 362x lower compute, and doubles live DFT hit rate on OE62 (33.3% vs. 16.7%) at 92.8x lower compute.

papers.title: Universal Work Extraction from Individual Sequences by Finite--State Information Engines
papers.summary: We consider information engines that interact with a heat bath at temperature $T$, a work reservoir, and a tape carrying an individual (deterministic) sequence $x$ over a finite alphabet $\X$. An engine is a cascade of autonomous ratchets with fixed energy levels and detailed--balance dynamics, each processing segments of $m$ tape cells and having finitely many internal states. We prove a converse bound on the extractable work in terms of the empirical block entropies of $x$,and show that it is achievable \emph{universally}, by engines whose energy levels do not depend on $x$. The maximal work per symbol is $kT[\ln|\X|-\bar H(x)]$, where $k$ is Boltzmann's constant and $\bar H(x)$ is the asymptotic normalized aligned block entropy of $x$, which equals its block Lempel--Ziv complexity, and the minimal work needed to erase $x$ is $kT\bar H(x)$ per symbol.
